::: {.block title="2. Is there hope for coastal regions?"}
![Left: R² by depth for profiles in open-ocean, slope and shelf water (ETOPO 2022 depth); bins with fewer than 3 floats or sites not drawn. Right: integrated Chl *a*, observed vs predicted. Held-out data, space-time split; model trained and scored on Argo + OOI data together.](figures/fig_coastal_skill.png){#fig-coastal script="scripts/fig_coastal_skill.py" width="100%"}

Skill falls with depth everywhere, and faster in shallow water: R² reaches
about 0 by 20 m on the shelf and by 50 m on the slope, but stays near 0.35
below 80 m in the open ocean. Integrated Chl *a* holds up better (R² 0.43 open,
0.35 slope, 0.33 shelf), because the upper bins carry most of it. Coastal
water is sampled mostly by fixed moorings, so few whole coastal profiles
exist to train or test on.

More importantly, ability to predict surface Chl in coastal regions depended on having trained on that region (OOI). In contrast, it was not needed to see areas of open ocean (Argo). Caveat is that we had limited coast sites (5 OOI).

| Data | Split | 0–10 m | 50–60 m | 100–110 m | Integrated |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Argo | Space-time | 0.75 | 0.58 | 0.38 | 0.32 |
| | New region | 0.74 | 0.56 | 0.35 | 0.26 |
| OOI | Space-time | 0.54 | −0.01 | −0.09 | 0.18 |
| | New region | 0.10 | −0.24 | −0.74 | −0.36 |

: R² of log10 Chl *a* on held-out data, models trained on each platform alone (mean of 5 repeats). Space-time: 1° × 30-day blocks held out; new region: 10° boxes held out. {#tbl-region}
